key_insight: In low-offset organic solar cells, charge separation efficiency is governed not just by the LE–CT energy gap, but also by state degeneracy and energetic disorder, which can even turn disorder into a benefit at small offsets.
engineering_relevance: Device design can use molecular energetics and controlled disorder to optimize internal quantum efficiency without requiring a large exciton-to-charge transfer driving force.
method: Compared a macroscopic two-state rate model against 3D kinetic Monte Carlo (kMC) simulations.
Varied the LE–CT offset across the full range and tested how degeneracy ratios shift the efficiency curves.
Introduced Gaussian energetic disorder in kMC to map when disorder helps or hurts charge separation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the analytical rate model matches kMC across all offsets without disorder, and that disorder shows a crossover: harmful at large offsets but beneficial at intermediate and low offsets.
watch_item: The disorder-assisted gains depend on the assumed Gaussian energetic disorder and thermalization behavior, so material-specific calibration is needed before using the trend for device design.
paper_title: Dependence of charge separation efficiency on the exciton-charge transfer offset and Gaussian disorder in organic solar cells
